propositions: The gate matches field names globally across all config reads, so a field with no read site passes if any unrelated config has a same-named attribute read anywhere in the tree.
CodeHealthConfig.enabled had zero read sites but passed the gate because UiConfig.enabled and other configs reuse the name 'enabled', putting it into a global set that satisfied the check.
A field is satisfied only when its OWNING dataclass is the receiver of the read, not when a same-named attribute on an unrelated config matches the bare terminal name.

The fixed gate resolves each read's receiver expression to its owning schema class through section attributes, parameter annotations, local assignment propagation, return type annotations, and cross-module fixed-point binding of call sites.

The four newly-flagged fields (McpConfig.readonly, McpConfig.allow_llm, McpConfig.allow_jira_sync, JiraConfig.allow_insecure) are all live reads through excluded plumbing or string keys; each receives a factual read-via marker naming its real consumer.
